subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in mode that runs a successful memory flush and then resets the session instead of compacting when context reaches the compaction threshold?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear in source, but choosing it affects session continuity, silent tool-capable memory writes, config defaults, provider routing, and security policy; automation should not pick that product boundary.

options.title: Approve a guarded opt-in mode
options.body: Add a default-off reset-after-flush config with explicit success criteria, timeout/cancel behavior, sandbox limits, audit/logging, and regression coverage for provider/auth routing and session rollover.

options.title: Keep compaction after flush
options.body: Treat pre-compaction memory flush as a durability aid only, keep compaction as the default recovery step, and close or narrow the reset-after-flush request as not planned.

options.title: Fold into reset-memory design
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45608 the policy venue for reset-time memory preservation and split only the compaction-threshold trigger if maintainers want a separate implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve a guarded opt-in mode
recommendation.body: Add a default-off reset-after-flush config with explicit success criteria, timeout/cancel behavior, sandbox limits, audit/logging, and regression coverage for provider/auth routing and session rollover.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the original pre-compaction flush and reset paths, so they are the best available owner for the cross-boundary lifecycle decision.
